event_text: USS Nevada is sunk by an aerial torpedo after surviving hits from two atomic bombs (as part of post-war tests) and being used for target practice by three other ships.
headline: USS Nevada Sunk in Operation Crossroads, 1948
story: Barry peered out at the wreckage, his beak twitching. 'Well, Susan, it seems the USS Nevada's had a bit of a rough patch. Survived not one, but two atomic bombs - Able and Baker, if you recall - as part of Operation Crossroads. And that was after being strafed by the USS Pennsylvania, pounded by the USS Iowa, and generally used as a target by the USS Indiana.' Susan snorted, ruffling her feathers. 'Target practice, how thrilling. And after all that, an aerial torpedo finally sends her to the bottom. I suppose it's a wonder she lasted this long.' Barry shrugged. 'Test of endurance, really. The US Navy wanted to see how much punishment a battleship could take. Nevada was the prime guinea pig, poor thing. Now she's a artificial reef, providing a home for marine life - a strange kind of victory, I suppose.' Susan gazed out at the sea, her expression dry. 'All in the name of science, of course. Because what's a few ships and some radiation poisoning when you're advancing human knowledge?'
regret_line: A tad more caution might have been in order, considering the lingering effects of radiation on the surrounding ecosystem.
winner_line: The concept of nuclear deterrence, which gained a significant amount of data from the operation, albeit at a steep environmental cost.
